multiplechoiceresponse.p: An assistant summarises a table and quotes a total. What is the minimum check?

choice.div: Recompute the total from the table and check the subgroup sums add up.
Ask the assistant whether it is sure.

div.p: Any number that will be quoted is recomputed. Group totals should reconcile to the whole, or the exclusions should be stated.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A chart shows a dramatic rise because the axis starts at 90 instead of 0. What is the problem?

choice.div: The visual exaggerates a small change; the caption must state the axis or the chart must be redrawn.
Nothing, as long as the data is accurate.
Truncated axes are always forbidden, with no exception.

div.p: A truncated axis can be legitimate for small variation, but it must not be presented as a large effect.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Why record cleaning decisions before analysing?

choice.div: So the result is reproducible and a challenged number has a defensible answer.
Because tools require a log file.

div.p: Row drops, imputations and duplicate rules change results. The record is what makes the analysis auditable.

choiceresponse.p: Which checks belong in an assisted analysis? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Profile the data before cleaning it.
Record every row dropped and why.
State the denominator in the chart caption.
Trust the summary because the model saw the whole table.

div.p: Speed comes from the assistant; defensibility comes from these checks.
